From 61d099ac4a7a8fb11ebdb6e2ec8d77f38e77362f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tyllis Xu <livelycarpet87@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 12:01:50 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: ibmvfc: Fix OOB access in
 ibmvfc_discover_targets_done()

A malicious or compromised VIO server can return a num_written value in the
discover targets MAD response that exceeds max_targets. This value is
stored directly in vhost->num_targets without validation, and is then used
as the loop bound in ibmvfc_alloc_targets() to index into disc_buf[], which
is only allocated for max_targets entries. Indices at or beyond max_targets
access kernel memory outside the DMA-coherent allocation.  The
out-of-bounds data is subsequently embedded in Implicit Logout and PLOGI
MADs that are sent back to the VIO server, leaking kernel memory.

Fix by clamping num_written to max_targets before storing it.

Fixes: 072b91f9c651 ("[SCSI] ibmvfc: IBM Power Virtual Fibre Channel Adapter Client Driver")
Reported-by: Yuhao Jiang <danisjiang@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tyllis Xu <LivelyCarpet87@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Dave Marquardt <davemarq@linux.ibm.com>
Acked-by: Tyrel Datwyler <tyreld@linux.ibm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260314170151.548614-1-LivelyCarpet87@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/ibmvscsi/ibmvfc.c b/drivers/scsi/ibmvscsi/ibmvfc.c
index a20fce04fe79..3dd2adda195e 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/ibmvscsi/ibmvfc.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/ibmvscsi/ibmvfc.c
@@ -4966,7 +4966,8 @@ static void ibmvfc_discover_targets_done(struct ibmvfc_event *evt)
 	switch (mad_status) {
 	case IBMVFC_MAD_SUCCESS:
 		ibmvfc_dbg(vhost, "Discover Targets succeeded\n");
-		vhost->num_targets = be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written);
+		vhost->num_targets = min_t(u32, be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written),
+					   max_targets);
 		ibmvfc_set_host_action(vhost, IBMVFC_HOST_ACTION_ALLOC_TGTS);
 		break;
 	case IBMVFC_MAD_FAILED:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

### Modifications in `drivers/scsi/ibmvscsi/ibmvfc.c`

- **Changed line 4969** (in function `ibmvfc_discover_targets_done`):  
  Replaced direct assignment of `be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written)` to `vhost->num_targets` with a clamped assignment using `min_t(u32, ... , max_targets)`.
  - **Before:** `vhost->num_targets = be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written);`
  - **After:** `vhost->num_targets = min_t(u32, be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written), max_targets);`

### Relationship between changes

This patch modifies only one file and one statement. The change is a security fix that prevents an out-of-bounds (OOB) memory access vulnerability. The OOB occurred because:

1. A malicious VIO server could report a `num_written` value larger than the allocated `disc_buf[]` size (`max_targets`).
2. The unchecked `num_written` was stored in `vhost->num_targets` and later used as a loop bound in `ibmvfc_alloc_targets()`, causing reads/writes beyond the DMA-coherent buffer.
3. The out-of-bounds data could then be leaked back to the server via Implicit Logout or PLOGI MADs.

By clamping `num_written` to `max_targets`, the patch ensures that the loop bound never exceeds the allocated array size, eliminating both the OOB access and the potential kernel memory leak.

Here is the commit message:
scsi: ibmvfc: Fix OOB access in
 ibmvfc_discover_targets_done()

A malicious or compromised VIO server can return a num_written value in the
discover targets MAD response that exceeds max_targets. This value is
stored directly in vhost->num_targets without validation, and is then used
as the loop bound in ibmvfc_alloc_targets() to index into disc_buf[], which
is only allocated for max_targets entries. Indices at or beyond max_targets
access kernel memory outside the DMA-coherent allocation.  The
out-of-bounds data is subsequently embedded in Implicit Logout and PLOGI
MADs that are sent back to the VIO server, leaking kernel memory.

Fix by clamping num_written to max_targets before storing it.

Fixes: 072b91f9c651 ("[SCSI] ibmvfc: IBM Power Virtual Fibre Channel Adapter Client Driver")
Reported-by: Yuhao Jiang <danisjiang@gmail.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tyllis Xu <LivelyCarpet87@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Dave Marquardt <davemarq@linux.ibm.com>
Acked-by: Tyrel Datwyler <tyreld@linux.ibm.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260314170151.548614-1-LivelyCarpet87@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the lack of validation on the `num_written` field received from the VIO server in the discover targets MAD response. The value is directly assigned to `vhost->num_targets` without being clamped to `max_targets`, which is the size of the `disc_buf[]` array. This allows a malicious or compromised VIO server to provide a value exceeding `max_targets`, leading to an out-of-bounds access when `vhost->num_targets` is used as a loop bound in `ibmvfc_alloc_targets()`. The erroneous out-of-bounds data can then be leaked to the VIO server via subsequent Implicit Logout or PLOGI MADs.

Here is the patch:
  **/
 static void ibmvfc_discover_targets_done(struct ibmvfc_event *evt)
 {
 	struct ibmvfc_host *vhost = evt->vhost;
 	struct ibmvfc_discover_targets *rsp = &evt->xfer_iu->discover_targets;
 	u32 mad_status = be16_to_cpu(rsp->common.status);
 	int level = IBMVFC_DEFAULT_LOG_LEVEL;
 
 	switch (mad_status) {
 	case IBMVFC_MAD_SUCCESS:
 		ibmvfc_dbg(vhost, "Discover Targets succeeded\n");
-		vhost->num_targets = be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written);
+		vhost->num_targets = min_t(u32, be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written),
+					   max_targets);
 		ibmvfc_set_host_action(vhost, IBMVFC_HOST_ACTION_ALLOC_TGTS);
 		break;
 	case IBMVFC_MAD_FAILED:
 		level += ibmvfc_retry_host_init(vhost);
 		ibmvfc_log(vhost, level, "Discover Targets failed: %s (%x:%x)\n",
 			   ibmvfc_get_cmd_error(be16_to_cpu(rsp->status), be16_to_cpu(rsp->error)),
 			   be16_to_cpu(rsp->status), be16_to_cpu(rsp->error));
 		break;
 	case IBMVFC_MAD_DRIVER_FAILED:
 		break;
 	default:
 		dev_err(vhost->dev, "Invalid Discover Targets response: 0x%x\n", mad_status);
 		ibmvfc_link_down(vhost, IBMVFC_LINK_DEAD);
 		break;
 	}
 
 	ibmvfc_free_event(evt);
 	wake_up(&vhost->work_wait_q);
 }

Root cause:
The bug is caused by the lack of validation on the `num_written` field received from the VIO server in the discover targets MAD response. The value is directly assigned to `vhost->num_targets` without being clamped to `max_targets`, which is the size of the `disc_buf[]` array. This allows a malicious or compromised VIO server to provide a value exceeding `max_targets`, leading to an out-of-bounds access when `vhost->num_targets` is used as a loop bound in `ibmvfc_alloc_targets()`. The erroneous out-of-bounds data can then be leaked to the VIO server via subsequent Implicit Logout or PLOGI MADs.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
vhost->num_targets = be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written);
for (i = 0; i < vhost->num_targets; i++) { ... disc_buf[i] ... }
Reason:
The first statement directly stores an untrusted value from the VIO server response into `vhost->num_targets` without checking it against `max_targets`, which is the actual allocated size of `disc_buf[]`. The second statement uses this uncontrolled value as the loop bound, causing an out-of-bounds read from `disc_buf[]` when `num_written` exceeds `max_targets`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
vhost->num_targets = min_t(u32, be32_to_cpu(rsp->num_written), max_targets);
Reason:
This replacement clamps the received `num_written` value to the maximum allowed number of targets (`max_targets`), ensuring that the subsequent loop in `ibmvfc_alloc_targets()` never accesses beyond the allocated `disc_buf[]` array, thereby preventing the out-of-bounds memory access and the subsequent data leak.
